sample_unit: participants (12 providers in a focus group; 21 patients in community engagement studios)
models_evaluated: novel prediction algorithm for first-time perinatal depression onset

links.outcome: Whether end-user input from patients and providers shaped algorithm development and implementation planning
links.effect: Focus group and engagement studio findings were incorporated into iterative algorithm development and informed an implementation pilot plan. Participants reported positively about their engagement.
links.quote: Qualitative findings were incorporated into iterative algorithm development and informed an implementation pilot plan.

links.outcome: Stakeholder views on variable completeness, interpretability, and acceptability to inform the use case
links.effect: Providers and patients agreed on the interpretability of the variables and suggested additional predictors. Patients wanted to discuss results with providers, while providers cited limited bandwidth.
links.quote: Providers and patients showed consensus on the interpretability of the prediction algorithm's variables and discussed additional variables believed to be predictive of depression to ensure its completeness.

screen.reason: Qualitative study involving clinicians and patients evaluating the acceptability, completeness, and interpretability of a perinatal depression risk prediction algorithm to inform implementation planning.
